facts.text: Tuxedo Park is a gated village in Orange County, NY, founded in 1885 by Pierre Lorillard IV as a private hunting reserve.
The village’s name comes from a Lenape word meaning “round foot” or “Wolf Clan”, reflecting indigenous heritage.
The Tuxedo Train Station, a Metro-North stop, and the historic library designed by Bruce Price are among the village’s preserved landmarks.
Three churches, a train station, a library, and a post office built in the 1880s still stand, with the Tuxedo Historical Society housed in one of the churches.
The village’s original cottages, built by Lorillard IV, were rented or sold to friends and family, setting a pattern of exclusive residential development.
